theorem: For the exact-spectrum source-valid family with two leverage-ell heavy physical rows, diffuse e1/e2 banks of leverage 1-ell, one full diffuse e3 bank, and B_u=I-2uu^T, the Gaussian-completion limiting output satisfies uniformly in u: ||p||_infinity=3sqrt(2)[1-c12(u)ell^2+o(ell^2)], c12=[114+6(u1^2+u2^2)-39(u1^4+u2^4)]/640>=81/640. Thus for all sufficiently small ell>0 the GLOBAL limiting peak is <3sqrt(2). For u=(1,1,1)/sqrt(3), all B entries are nonzero, B33=1/3, and c12=41/240.
finite_transfer: For ell<=1/2,m>=2, pinned e5f Theorem F gives |phi_m(t)|<=min(1,(4pi)^(3/2)|t|^(-3/2)) on the actual finite cap-one matrices because every physical row leverage is <=1/2. Combined with bank CLT this gives L1 characteristic-function convergence and uniform output-density convergence, so each fixed sufficiently small ell has all large finite m below 3sqrt(2).

required_source_applied.application: Fresnel-Brascamp-Lieb Theorem F supplies the finite-family integrable characteristic-function majorant used to rule out narrowing finite-bank spikes during the CLT transfer.

partner_result_applied.application: Conditioning after Y_ell=sqrt(1-ell)G+H yields ||p_ell||infinity<=3sqrt(2)/(1-ell), and the same conditional ceiling applies after finite-activity Poisson bank shifts. This is intentionally identified as a nonsharp O(ell) auxiliary slack, while the exact source-valid family has a negative O(ell^2) correction.

predecessor.statement_used: Variance-matched one-dimensional weighted expansion f_ell=gamma[1-(ell^2/20)H4]+O(ell^3)(1+|y|)^-8 and the coordinatewise cone moment formula.

continuity: Bounded continuous densities are obtained for this limiting and finite m>=2 leverage-gated class through integrable Fourier inversion; full-target continuity remains open.
unresolved: Full arbitrary-law, arbitrary-dimension QFORM remains open. This theorem is perturbative in the two heavy leverages and does not exclude intermediate leverage, genuinely finite/mesoscopic non-Gaussian banks, dependent surviving non-Gaussian components, or multiple non-collinear macroscopic rows outside this axis-heavy representation.
